newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli Treasury 1997 inflation target 7-10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Israeli Treasury 1997 inflation target 7-10 pct.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Dan Merdior said on Monday that the government's inflation target for next year was 7-10 percent.

Sources at the Bank of Israel said the central bank had agreed to the target but that the two sides would be having further discussions on related issues this evening with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The sources said the central bank would advocate setting multi-year inflation targets, or at least a target for 1998. They said an annual target did not give the bank the six-to- nine-month lead time it needs to formulate appropriate monetary policy.

Meridor made known the target at a meeting with senior executives of Israel Corp. He told them there was a reasonable chance of bringing down inflation in 1997 "if we behave correctly and we behave with great caution."

The 1996 inflation target was 8-10 per percent, but in the first 11 months consumer prices have risen 9.7 percent. Although inflation fell in the second half of the year, Israel Discount Bank said in a recent report that it expected it to reach 10-11 percent next year.
The Bank of Israel has said it wants the inflation target to fall to 4-7 percent by the year 2000.
